sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
HVAX integrates design, procurement, installation, testing, commissioning and validation for cleanrooms, HVAC and controlled environments. Customers in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, healthcare and hospitals buy a compliant functioning installation, not a recurring subscription. Bought-out equipment and common-director suppliers are economically important. Krew adds hospital/laboratory instruments. Promoter-controlled Forgex, PNX and earlier HVAX Engineering/Isovax are not automatically subsidiaries owned by the listed company. [S1][S3][S12]

FY26 parent goods revenue was ₹152.6118 crore, services ₹5.2741 crore and other operating revenue ₹2.3221 crore, versus ₹96.5467/₹33.0247/₹1.4605 crore in FY25. This large mix shift means reported sales growth is not a direct volume or pricing-power measure. Overseas revenue of ₹125.0798 crore was 78.07% of parent revenue. Uganda ₹40.6994 crore, Kenya ₹24.9594 crore and Ghana ₹21.9107 crore were significant; Kenya fell from ₹51.8880 crore. Country exposure is not customer identity. FY24 top-ten customers contributed 69.10%, while top-ten suppliers supplied 56.14%; a current equivalent concentration table remains ND. [S1][S3]

Revenue recognition is a key audit matter under AS 9. The auditor describes testing contracts, dispatches, completion evidence and subsequent collections. This is relevant counterevidence but does not eliminate overdue-balance risk. Project milestones create a funding interval between procurement and receipt of cash. Backlog, pipeline, recognized sales and collected cash remain distinct. [S3]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Proposed moat: engineering and validation expertise → access to regulated tenders and customer relationships → time needed to qualify teams and deliver compliant projects → failure when competitors provide equivalent quality with better pricing, funding or delivery. The evidence supports useful specialization, not a demonstrated structural monopoly. Certifications, prestigious customers and order books alone are insufficient. No independently verified market-share denominator or durable price premium was found. [S1][S3][S10]

Relevant comparators, not an unverified peer-multiple target:
- Integrated Cleanroom Technologies is a larger, technically supported competitor. CARE’s April 2026 rationale reports FY25 consolidated operating income of ₹1,015.45 crore, PBILDT of ₹92.95 crore, CARE A/Stable and 96.5% Takasago ownership. Parent support and liquidity strengthen its position, although milestone working capital remains lengthy. [P3]
- Fabtech Cleanrooms, a separate listed manufacturer/integrator, reported FY26 group revenue of ₹219.3242 crore, PAT of ₹15.8153 crore and CFO of −₹13.4929 crore. Standalone revenue grew only 1.92% and PAT declined 24.78%. Acquisitions and manufacturing change the comparison. [P1]
- Fabtech Technologies, not Fabtech Cleanrooms, reported FY26 consolidated operations of ₹410.7718 crore and PAT of ₹38.3580 crore. Investment/exceptional gains and international operations require normalization; standalone CFO was −₹1.3617 crore. Its Ind AS basis also differs from HVAX. [P2]

There is a stronger funded competitor and cash-constrained peer evidence. Neither excuses HVAX’s cash conversion nor establishes exact peer rankings. Management itself acknowledged uncertainty about margins in new semiconductor/renewable-sector work. [S8]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
GQS is NS: known weighted contribution 5.20, coverage 85%, and CAP missing. Persistent CASH 2 creates a cap of 5 without manufacturing a point score. Strong sales growth cannot substitute for attractive incremental returns and realized cash. [E02][E03][E18]

Scaling depends on project teams, procurement, qualification, acceptance and collections. The FY26 report claims 165 professionals and 300+ projects over the company’s history, not 300 annual projects. Reported backlog of ₹365.25 crore is about 2.28 times parent FY26 revenue, but executable scheduling, cancellations, pricing protections and advances were not fully established. The ₹768.54 crore pipeline is not contracted revenue. The MD letter’s ₹57.87 crore “current year” revenue has no clear period; it is not substituted for audited annual revenue. [S3]

Base assumptions are 18/18/16/14/12/10% growth through FY27–FY32, EBIT margin rising from 10% to 11.5%, ONWC/revenue declining from 70% to 60%, and cash capex of 1% of sales. Bull assumes 25/25/22/20/18/15% growth, 14% EBIT margin and 48% terminal ONWC/revenue. Bear combines an initial 15% sales decline, 5.5–7% EBIT margin, sticky 80–86% ONWC and ₹10 crore initial-year debt repayment. These are analyst scenarios, not management forecasts. Their full annual funding paths are embedded.

No attributable project/cohort return or post-acquisition Krew investment return is verified. The 3.67% incremental portfolio proxy is disclosed but remains lag-misaligned and cannot score CAP. At base terminal economics, working capital alone requires roughly 60 paise per additional revenue rupee. Collections and financing must accompany margin and sales progress. [S2][S3]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held a combined 66.64% at March 2026; the October master confirms unchanged total issued shares. No substantiated severe diversion finding was found. Statutory and internal-financial-control opinions were unmodified, with no identified material fraud/default. These findings are retained but do not independently validate every control or RPT. Current pledge and late instrument information is not fully authenticated. [S3][M1]

Forgex purchases of ₹36.0172 crore represent 29.77% of parent purchases/labour. Common directors and no listed-company equity ownership in Forgex are disclosed. Directors’ pay of ₹2.58 crore equals 18.04% of parent PAT, with related-family salaries and PNX rent/professional fees additional. The company says dealings are ordinary-course and arm’s-length; no independent pricing benchmark was found. Board text saying no material RPT conflicts with the disclosed size. The PNX resolution says ₹75 crore, while its explanation says ₹2 crore. The actual AGM filing records passage of the related agenda, but does not resolve that textual contradiction. [S3][S11]

₹150 crore borrowing authority is shareholder permission, not an available line. Krew’s 80% acquisition for ₹1.40 crore completed on 26 March 2026; the earlier draft term sheet was only a proposal. AOC-1’s prior-year heading and 0% holding contradict the acquisition note and need correction. Parent/group differences themselves are not errors. [S3][S7]

Internal-audit reports were unavailable to statutory auditors despite the appointment of internal auditors and positive control opinion. Those precise limitations are preserved. [S3]

FY21 was positive and FY26 burn improved versus FY25, but poor realization remains persistent. Restated FY22–24 numbers form a distinct series with the prospectus’s income/expense, tax and opening debtor-write-off explanation. Their differences alone are not a G2 failure. [S1][S2][S3][S5][S6]

FX-neutral operating EBIT falls from ₹17.4373 crore to ₹15.2273 crore. Export FX is economically relevant, and the realized/unrealized split is ND: zero FX is a scenario, not corrected audited earnings. Consolidated PAT of ₹14.7301 crore differs from owners’ PAT of ₹14.3096 crore; use the latter for equity P/E. [S2][S3]

Average AR days are 178.03 versus 134.18. Inventory days of 108.84 and payable days of 53.49 produce a 233.37-day CCC proxy. Total revenue, material/service cost and purchases/labour are labeled denominator proxies, not perfectly matched credit bases. Over-six-months-due AR of ₹54.9082 crore includes ₹33.3048 crore older than a year. Management calls these good and undisputed. FY25 ageing contains a negative ₹0.6171 crore two-to-three-year bucket, and its under-six-months total differs from note 15. No loss percentage is invented. [S3]

G2 hold: June/December 2025 bank-versus-books debtor differences are ₹16.4192/₹12.3750 crore. March reconciliation “books” shows ₹86.8767 crore versus statement ₹84.8442 crore. CARO p80 nevertheless says bank returns agree, while consolidated p152 says they were not maintained/made available and not reconciled. Internal-audit reports were unavailable (p84). sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The thesis-break variable is converting aged project receivables into unrestricted cash. Customer/country disruption → slower acceptance and collections → inventory/receivable absorption → less bank headroom → forced fundraising or curtailed execution → margin damage and per-share dilution. A successfully installed project can still impair shareholders if payment is late or uncollectible. [S3]

Bear assumptions combine an initial 15% sales decline, working capital of 80–86% of sales, EBIT margins of 5.5–7% and ₹10 crore initial-year debt repayment. Gross rescue equity is ₹11.15 crore. Its conditional terminal price of ₹216.32 is 70.08% below the quote, before unknown impact. This is not a liquidation recovery promise. A cash-floor breach invalidates the ordinary path even if accounting earning power remains positive.

The strongest argument against the hold is genuine sales expansion, experienced project execution, banking relationships, positive profits, clean opinions and management’s reconciliation explanations. Milestone collections could improve cash materially. These facts are retained. They do not settle contradictory bank disclosures or produce current funding letters. High impairment risk is not a claim of inevitable default or fraud.

A price decline alone would not clear G2/G3. Auditor-backed bridges, collection evidence and financed incremental growth could change the conclusion; routine quote volatility would not.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
No multibagger recommendation is supported. A five-year 5x price outcome requires about 37.97% annual growth; 10x requires about 58.49%. The explicit-rescue bull can approach 5x only with strong sales growth, 14% EBIT margin, major working-capital improvement and a 16x terminal EBIT multiple. It is not an ordinary funded case. A 10x result would require substantially more intrinsic value per share and is Speculative / unsupported.

The correct decomposition is revenue growth × attributable net-margin change × current/future diluted shares × terminal/current P/E, with dividends separate. Reported FX gains and unknown funding make an EV-to-equity bridge more appropriate here. A ₹365 crore backlog, ₹769 crore pipeline or small market cap does not establish a multibagger without collections, capital and dilution support. [S3]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS are all NS. The matrix cannot assign an investment cell from missing-factor midpoints. G2/G3/G4 holds take priority; G1 is Conditional, not Fail. No governance or funding-failure numeric cap is invented. The only applied cap is GQS ≤5 for persistent CASH 2, and missing remains missing. Ranking eligibility is false for all three aggregates. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate.

Action category: Research priority / unresolved-evidence hold, not a favorable new-investment conclusion. Resolve bank/books and cash-flow bridges, verify current funding and aged-debtor collections, establish attributable incremental returns and complete the implementation evidence. A cheaper reported P/E or a better rescue scenario alone would not clear those requirements.

There is no ordinary entry range or supported ordinary return. Rescue fees, issue price and dilution are counterfactual, not arranged financing. The ₹5 lakh illustration is not an allocation recommendation. For an existing holding, this identifies reliability, funding, normalization and liquidity questions; it does not instruct a buy, sale or reduction without the holder’s circumstances.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The evidence ledger distinguishes verified disclosures (V), reproducible calculations (C), attributed management statements (M) and analyst assumptions (A). “Verified disclosure” means checked in the actual document, not independent assurance of realizability. Original, restated, parent and group accounts remain distinct. Unmodified opinions and management explanations are preserved beside material limitations.

Key open questions:
1. Reconcile quarterly bank submissions, customer ledgers and the March statement, including the ₹2.0325 crore debtor difference.
2. Explain why CARO says returns agree while note 33 says they were unavailable/unreconciled. Supply the missing internal-audit reports.
3. Establish current unrestricted cash, drawable facilities, maturities, renewals and collections. March cash and a ₹150 crore authority are not substitutes.
4. Split realized/unrealized FX, related taxes and hedging effects.
5. Reconcile Krew’s acquisition-date cash, post-control earnings, capital profit, minority interest and the AOC-1 holding/date errors.
6. Supply independent RPT price evidence and the correct PNX ceiling; explain the board report’s materiality wording.
7. Verify current pledges, warrants, convertibles, ESOPs and contingent commitments beyond March declarations.
